title: On-delay and off-delay in Ladder: timers as blocks in a rung
summary: Place a TOF and a TON between a contact and a coil, and see that an off-delay keeps a light on after the button and an on-delay ignores a sensor that does not stay on.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence with one 10 ms task; they do not establish real sensor filtering requirements, wiring, hardware timing, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Place a timer function block in a rung, with the contact feeding its IN and its output feeding the coil.
Tell an off-delay (TOF) from an on-delay (TON) by what each does when the input rises and falls.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/DelaysLd.ld.json two rungs connect a contact straight to a coil. Insert a TOF of T#300ms in the first rung, so that Light stays on for T#300ms after Button is released, and a TON of T#200ms in the second, so that Confirmed turns on only after Sensor has been on for T#200ms.
stages.checkpoint: Each rung has contact, timer and coil in that order.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Button is pressed at {{t:100}} ms and released at {{t:300}} ms. Sensor is on from {{t:100}} to {{t:140}} ms, and again from {{t:500}} to {{t:900}} ms. Predict Light at {{t:450}} and {{t:650}} ms and Confirmed at {{t:450}} and {{t:800}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:DelaysLd.Light=true@450|ON}} at {{t:450}} ms, still inside the T#300ms hold; {{v:DelaysLd.Light=false@650|OFF}} at {{t:650}} ms; {{v:DelaysLd.Confirmed=false@450|OFF}} at {{t:450}} ms, because the pulse was too short; {{v:DelaysLd.Confirmed=true@800|ON}} at {{t:800}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press Check: The starter has no timers: Light drops the moment Button is released and Confirmed follows Sensor, so Light is OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed is ON at {{t:120}} ms; place a TOF of T#300ms between Button and Light, and a TON of T#200ms between Sensor and Confirmed. From the toolbox drag a TOF block into the first rung and a TON into the second, between the contact and the coil, and set PT on each.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named DelaysLd and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare Light at {{t:300}} and {{t:650}} ms with Confirmed at {{t:140}} and {{t:800}} ms: the TOF delays the fall of its input, the TON delays the rise.
stages.checkpoint: Light falls once, after the hold, and Confirmed rises once, after the sensor has stayed on for T#200ms; the short pulse at {{t:100}} ms never raises it.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Swap the two blocks, TON for the hold and TOF for the filter, and see which assertions fail. What does each block do to a short pulse?
stages.checkpoint: A TON ignores a pulse shorter than its preset and a TOF stretches a pulse by its preset. A real sensor filter also needs a preset chosen against the real signal, which this scenario does not measure.

hints.text: The coil must not see the contact directly. Which block sits between them, and what does each of the two blocks do to a signal?
In the first rung place a TOF with PT T#300ms and in the second a TON with PT T#200ms, each between its contact and its coil, and leave IN connected to the contact.

faultCases: The starter has no timers: Light drops the moment Button is released and Confirmed follows Sensor, so Light is OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed is ON at {{t:120}} ms; place a TOF of T#300ms between Button and Light, and a TON of T#200ms between Sensor and Confirmed.
